 1.

The petitioner no. 1 is the married sister-in-law of the victim and the petitioner no. 2 is the husband
of the petitioner no. 1.
2.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that they have been falsely implicated in the instant case.
It is further submitted that the victim and her husband were married for almost 33 years according to Muslim rites and customs.

3. Learned counsel for the State in opposing the prayer for anticipatory bail has referred to the statement of the neighbours recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C and submits that the petitioners are also involved in the commission of the crime.
However, it is submitted that the husband of the victim and some other co-accused persons have been arrested and subsequently granted bail.
It is further submitted that still two more persons are absconding and their prayer for anticipatory bail is Indian Penal Code vs In Re: Taiyaba Bibi @ Taiba Bibi @ Sahida ...

The post-mortem report shows that the death was due to the effect of injury ante mortem in nature.

4. Considering the nature of involvement of the present petitioners in the commission of alleged offence and the fact that the charge-sheet has already been filed, we are of the view that custodial interrogation of the petitioners are not necessary.

5. Accordingly, we direct that in the event of arrest, the petitioners Taiyaba Bibi @ Taiba Bibi @
Sahida Bibi and Sk. Mahammad shall be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs.10,000/-each, with two registered sureties of like amount each, subject to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer and also to comply with the conditions as laid down in Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
